findings.severity: MAJOR (crash site outside the named closure)
findings.claim: dispatch_tool routes the non-read-only doctor through execute_through_bridge -> bridge.execute -> _execute_houdini (shared/bridge.py), which runs _compute_scene_hash (hou.node/sessionId/intrinsics), _undo_evidence_snapshot (hou.undos.areEnabled), and `with hou.undos.group()` BARE on the calling thread and only RECORDS main_thread_executed (does not marshal). Off-main that is the F1 crash class, in a module OUTSIDE the store/doctor closure AND outside my touches (shared/ is INTEGRATOR territory). The undo group is structurally coupled to op.fn (a context manager cannot straddle threads), so the doctor CANNOT be split off-main while bridge-routed.
findings.handling: Target 3 BYPASSES the bridge for the doctor (handler.handle directly), so _execute_houdini is never on the off-main doctor path. The doctor mutates nothing, so the bridge integrity wrap is pure overhead; the LIVE-path envelope block (observe-only) still fires on the handler.handle path only where enveloped -- and the doctor is in ENVELOPE_SKIP_COMMANDS, so it leaves FloorGate Tier-0 provenance, not a bridge IntegrityBlock. This is the in-scope way to close F2 without editing shared/bridge.py.

findings.claim: Bypassing the bridge means the in-Houdini /mcp doctor response no longer carries a bridge `_integrity` block (it did when bridge-routed). Headless already had none (get_bridge()->None), so this ALIGNS the in-Houdini path with headless rather than diverging it. C5 lock + FloorGate provenance are preserved; the mission asked to preserve 'C5 lock/provenance', not the bridge IntegrityBlock.

for_ruling.question: The off-main doctor dispatch bypasses execute_through_bridge for synapse_doctor (F2/F3), which is the only in-scope way to make it off-main-safe without editing shared/bridge.py (INTEGRATOR territory). Is bypassing the bridge for a zero-mutation diagnostic the accepted design, or should the doctor instead be declared bridge-read-only in panel/bridge_adapter._READ_ONLY_TOOLS (a panel-territory change) so dispatch_tool takes handler.handle itself?
for_ruling.why_human: It is a routing/ownership decision touching another agent's territory (bridge_adapter is panel/; shared/bridge.py is INTEGRATOR). The in-mcp-server.py bypass keeps the change inside W2-S1's touches; the bridge_adapter declaration would be cleaner but crosses a file-ownership boundary. Either is defensible; the choice is architectural.

for_ruling.question: Secondary pxr (F4): the off-main dispatch moves moneta_provenance pxr reads AND the external-Moneta store construct off Houdini's main thread. pxr has no main-thread affinity so this is judged safe, but the external Moneta authoring is unverifiable here. Ship as-is (probe-gated), or gate the off-main dispatch behind a probe of the external Moneta pkg first?
for_ruling.why_human: Cost/benefit of shipping a hou-safe fix whose secondary pxr exposure is verified-by-reasoning but not verified-by-probe against an external package. Agent position: ship -- the hou F1 fix is the mission and is fully verified; the pxr exposure is a lesser class and is spawn-probed (S1P1).
